Get Wikipedia articles for a location

Source: R/get_wiki_data.R
get_wiki_data.Rd

Use the Wikipedia geosearch API to get Wikipedia articles near a location. Only articles with coordinates are returned. See the GeoData extension https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Extension:GeoData and the API documentation for the geosearch module https://www.mediawiki.org/w/api.php?action=help&modules=query%2Bgeosearch for more information.

Usage

get_wiki_data(
  location,
  radius = FALSE,
  primary = NULL,
  details = NULL,
  limit = 50,
  list = "geosearch",
  lang = getOption("getdata.lang", default = "en"),
  geometry = TRUE,
  dist = getOption("getdata.dist"),
  diag_ratio = getOption("getdata.diag_ratio"),
  unit = getOption("getdata.unit", "meter"),
  asp = getOption("getdata.asp"),
  crs = getOption("getdata.crs", 3857),
  remove_coords = TRUE,
  clean_names = TRUE
)

Arguments

location

sf object. If multiple areas are provided, they are unioned into a single sf object using sf::st_union()

radius

If TRUE, use dist as a buffer around the center of the location; defaults to FALSE. If numeric, the value is used as dist and radius is set to TRUE.

primary

If NULL, search for primary coordinates. Set primary to "all" or "secondary" to search other coordinate types.

details

Additional details to return with results. Options include "name", "type", "dim", "scale", "region", "country", and "globe"; defaults to NULL.

limit

Number of pages to return (max 500); defaults to 50

list

method to use for query; "geosearch" returns data, "resp" returns response

lang

Language to search on Wikipedia; defaults to "en".

geometry

If TRUE (default), return sf object. If FALSE, return data frame.

dist

buffer distance in units. Optional.

diag_ratio

ratio of diagonal distance of area's bounding box used as buffer distance. e.g. if the diagonal distance is 3000 meters and the "diag_ratio = 0.1" a 300 meter will be used. Ignored when dist is provided.

unit

Units for buffer. Supported options include "meter", "foot", "kilometer", and "mile", "nautical mile" Common abbreviations (e.g. "km" instead of "kilometer") are also supported. Distance in units is converted to units matching GDAL units for x; defaults to "meter"

asp

Aspect ratio of width to height as a numeric value (e.g. 0.33) or character (e.g. "1:3"). If numeric, get_asp() returns the same value without modification.

crs

Coordinate reference system of bounding box to return; defaults to NULL which maintains the crs of the input object.

remove_coords

For df_to_sf(), if TRUE, remove the coordinate columns after converting a data frame to simple feature object; defaults to FALSE.

clean_names

If TRUE, clean names provided to nm or created based on value of col using janitor::clean_names. If FALSE, use names as provided.

Details

This function only covers the geosearch module. It returns the page ID, title, coordinates, and distance from the search point for each article (plus optional coordinate details) but not article text, extracts, images, categories, or Wikidata properties such as height or construction date. It also only searches one language edition of Wikipedia at a time and does not search other Wikimedia projects (e.g. Wikidata or Wikimedia Commons).

For this function, location can be either an sf, sfc, or bbox object or the title of a Wikipedia article with a related location. If location is an sf object, the search is made using the bounding box of the location (adjusted by dist, diag_ratio, and asp) or, if radius = TRUE, a circle around the center of the location. The API limits the search area: a radius must be between 10 and 10,000 meters and a bounding box can't be much larger than about 25 kilometers across.

See also

GNfindNearbyWikipedia() and GNwikipediaBoundingBox() functions in the geonames package

Examples

# Get articles within a radius of a point
bmore_city_hall <- sf::st_sfc(
  sf::st_point(c(-76.6122, 39.2904)),
  crs = 4326
)

get_wiki_data(
  location = bmore_city_hall,
  radius = TRUE,
  dist = 500,
  limit = 5
)
#> New names:
#> • `` -> `...1`
#> Simple feature collection with 5 features and 5 fields
#> Geometry type: POINT
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: -8528526 ymin: 4763254 xmax: -8528371 ymax: 4763417
#> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>     pageid    ns title                    dist primary           geometry
#> *    <int> <int> <chr>                   <dbl> <chr>          <POINT [m]>
#> 1 14963519     0 Battle Monument          37.7 ""      (-8528455 4763397)
#> 2 81206170     0 Equitable Building (Ba…  47.9 ""      (-8528489 4763333)
#> 3 17302400     0 Baltimore City Circuit…  66.5 ""      (-8528371 4763416)
#> 4 21451830     0 One Calvert Plaza        77.8 ""      (-8528431 4763254)
#> 5 21562114     0 United States Post Off…  88   ""      (-8528526 4763417)

# A numeric radius is used as dist (set unit to change the distance unit)
get_wiki_data(
  location = bmore_city_hall,
  radius = 0.25,
  unit = "mi",
  limit = 5
)
#> ℹ Using `radius` value of 0.25 for `dist`.
#> ✔ Setting `radius` to TRUE.

#> • `` -> `...1`

# Search within the bounding box of a polygon or other sf object
bmore_area <- sf::st_buffer(
  sf::st_transform(bmore_city_hall, 26985),
  dist = 300
)

get_wiki_data(
  location = bmore_area,
  limit = 5
)

# Return additional coordinate details for each article
get_wiki_data(
  location = bmore_city_hall,
  radius = TRUE,
  dist = 500,
  details = c("type", "name"),
  limit = 5
)

# Return a data frame with longitude and latitude columns instead of an sf
# object
get_wiki_data(
  location = bmore_city_hall,
  radius = TRUE,
  dist = 500,
  limit = 5,
  geometry = FALSE,
  remove_coords = FALSE
)

# Return the full API response instead of a data frame
resp <- get_wiki_data(
  location = bmore_city_hall,
  radius = TRUE,
  dist = 500,
  limit = 2,
  list = "resp"
)
#> New names:
#> • `` -> `...1`
